newsitem.title: UK: BA works with cargo clients for efficiency.
newsitem.headline: BA works with cargo clients for efficiency.

text.p: LONDON, July 14 (Reuters ) - British Airways Plc World Cargo division plans to restructure customer relationships, sharing joint responsibilities for the efficient movement of freight, the airline's in-house magazine said.

Electronic commerce will feature prominently in achieving this, with a goal of 85 percent of all cargo arriving ready to carry when BA's new 250 million pound ($422.4 million) cargo centre opens in January 1998, it said.

Documentation will be exchanged electronically and shipments bar-coded, boosted by a 34 million pound investment in information systems - a 283 percent increase over 1995, the magazine said in a report on BA's recent internal World Cargo conference at Gatwick.
There will also be a new UK call centre to be ready by November.

The report said initiatives disclosed at the conference include the "Tail to Tail" project with 50 stations worldwide involved in securing high-yield cargo, and a new capacity management system allowing staff to identify the highest-value traffic and its suitability in terms of size, shape, commodity and connection times. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com ($ = 0.591 British Pounds)
